folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_chain.he: A meal order: flour, dough, noodles and the finished dish
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_chain.te: Order the final dish, such as udon noodles, and register every station along its route. The colony plans the needed intermediate foods instead of asking you to order each one by hand.
Wheat becomes flour in the real millstone. Keep the turning path and a clear exit open: the resident must finish driving the mill and walk free before another step can use the output.
The normal crafting recipe combines flour and a water bucket into raw dough. That intermediate is real inventory, and the empty bucket returns through the same ordinary crafting logistics.

A borrowed kitchen knife cuts that dough on the actual chopping board. The native recipe gives three raw noodles; the knife returns for another task, and the real surplus noodles remain available for later orders.

The stockpot route also needs its real soup base, lettuce, egg, lid and bowl. Fixed and flexible recipes may require different quantities, so a shorter ingredient list still follows native matching and quality rules.
The final order completes with the actual served dish. No station is skipped, and missing ingredients, a borrowed tool or an unfinished native timer keep the dependent step waiting.

Other chains obey their own native conditions too: drying needs the right exposure, steaming needs heat and a closed lid, and tea needs real brewing and serving. Provide the stations, safe paths and base materials; the colony carries each real intermediate between them.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_equipmen: A hat in the pack has no seed effect. A grass-seed gathering task borrows one allowed straw hat, equips it and returns it afterward. Ordinary farming and kitchen work do not request a hat.

Clothing has its own allowlist. Relevant water-farming tasks may borrow a complete farmer set and return it afterward. An unrelated equipped item is never replaced. Disabling the task or clothing returns the borrowed pieces.
A farm normally uses Pick: tea regrows from age three, tomato and chili from age five. Open that plot's Harvest mode setting and choose Sickle for native whole-harvest loot and young regrowth.

The sickle is borrowed for this task. Residents cut the claimed root without sweeping a neighbor's land. Mature crops, the blacklist, sweep-enchantment wear and the ten-tick cooldown still apply; rice is counted once.

Knives, spatulas and sickles are shared colony tools. One missing tool may be made from raw materials; a tool already borrowed makes other work wait. Return it to an available rack or warehouse after the task. Maintain orders can provide more.
Only four genuinely equipped farmer pieces activate Cookery's water movement effect. Water tasks borrow the complete set together and return it afterward; the hat alone only enables seed loot.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_heat.hea: Kitchen heat: light, shelter and relight
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_heat.tex: Mark the stove as a kitchen station. The colony tends its ignition separately from the food cooking above it.
Lighting spends one flint-and-steel durability, or one fire charge. A native stove keeps burning without a coal slot or repeated fuel deliveries.
Cooking follows the appliance's native heat rules: lit heat sources, or blocks in its heat-source tag such as magma, can supply heat.
Rain or water can put the stove out. Residents wait for a dry, reachable stove instead of wasting ignition items repeatedly.
Keep the interaction side and a standing place clear. Once the shelter is dry, the colony can relight the stove and cooking can continue.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_millston: The millstone: drive it, release it, walk clear
The nine millstone parts belong to one kitchen station. A flour order can fetch wheat and arrange a real grinding task.
Leave a reachable exit and room for the resident to circle the mill. The task checks its way out before loading any ingredients.
Passing residents are not captured. Only the assigned resident may bind as the motor; the native mill then turns and processes the actual input.
Finished grinding releases the motor immediately. The task still waits until the resident really walks clear; unbinding in place is not a completed exit.
Only then are the real output slots emptied into colony logistics. The same flour is never also left as a loose duplicate.
Cancellation and reload release the resident safely and preserve accepted ingredients for recovery. A blocked exit waits for a path; ordinary animal-driven mills keep their native behavior.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_orders.h: A colony kitchen: order the final dish
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_orders.t: Mark the kitchen stations, a crafting table and storage with the colony book. Keep a reachable place to stand beside each appliance.
Give residents the crafting trade, then set a delivery or maintain-stock order for the finished dish. The colony arranges the ingredients and intermediate steps.
Keep base ingredients, containers and reusable kitchen tools in accessible stores. A missing ingredient or blocked appliance leaves the task waiting without spending its inputs.
The Kitchen page shows each registered appliance and its current state. Use its lessons to learn heat, shared tools, milling, cooking and farming.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_pots.hea: Pots and stockpots: real ingredients, heat and serving vessels
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_pots.tex: Register each pot or stockpot as a kitchen station and keep its heat source lit. Leave the handle side of a stir-fry pot clear: the resident works immediately beside its handle. Players' existing ingredients and dishes are left alone.
A stir-fry batch checks all its food, one oil and any serving vessels before loading. It then uses the real pot to add oil and ingredients; containers returned by those ingredients rejoin storage.

The resident borrows a real kitchen shovel and performs the recipe's native stirs. Cooking runs on the block's own timer. A dish with serving vessels needs its complete vessel count; other products are taken with the shovel.

Stir-fry must be collected within its native 40-second window. It then burns, and after another 20 seconds becomes real charcoal. A long interruption can lose the requested dish: spent ingredients are not refunded and the original food is not recreated.

A stockpot batch checks its actual soup base, food, lid and vessels together. The resident fills the base, adds ingredients and closes the real lid; the native cooking timer then advances while heat and lid are present.

Open the stockpot and serve each actual portion with its required vessel. Three rice portions spend three bowls, not six. The same real lid can serve later batches, and the next batch begins only after the previous one is fully collected.

Fixed recipes and flexible recipes use the native matching rules. Flexible dishes keep the quality calculated by the actual appliance. Accepted batches survive cancellation and reload; recovery takes the owned result rather than spending the ingredients again.

Normal orders use matching native recipes. Only an explicit Suspicious Stir-Fry or Dark Cuisine order chooses unmatched ingredients. Suspicious Stir-Fry is served after cooking; only a Dark Cuisine order waits for the real burnt state. An accidentally burnt normal dish does not complete its original order.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_rice.hea: Rice: from a flooded plot to a bowl
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_rice.tex: Mark a flooded dirt plot with the colony book and supply a hoe. Residents till its soil before sowing; suitable existing farmland also works. Keep water in the bottom crop space and two clear spaces above.
One physical wild rice seed plants all three parts. Residents prefer wild seeds; edible rice can plant the same crop when it is the available fallback.
A mature plant is one harvest. Only its bottom part yields panicles and wild seeds; the two upper parts are claimed with it, so they never pay the harvest again.
Ordinary harvesting leaves water for the next planting. Replanting spends a real harvested seed. Wild seeds and edible rice share one planting reserve, with wild seeds kept first.
Mark a reachable millstone as a kitchen station. A rice order can send a resident to drive the real mill: one panicle supplies three grains, and the resident walks safely out when finished.
Order the finished rice meal. Residents connect the paddy, millstone and heated stockpot themselves. Supply the recipe's bowls and lid; missing carriers wait instead of spending the next batch.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_seeds.he: Keep seeds, compost surplus, restore grass
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_seeds.te: Register a Seed grass area with the colony book. A farmer wearing a real straw hat gathers its short grass only while obtainable grass seeds are missing. A hat does not create seeds without a real source.

Drops use the original loot chances. Keep a rare first seed for expansion: sow it, grow it and collect its real offspring. Other seeds need their own farms or valid conversion recipes; short grass cannot supply every crop.

The Composting settings page controls automatic composting, a default seed reserve (64), and individual values for seeds the colony owns or grows. Sowing, goods in transit, task claims and explicit orders remain protected. Wild rice and rice share one reserve entry, with wild seeds kept first.

Mark a composter. Composting needs no straw hat. Planning checks surplus before each batch, which spends the average native input count to fill level seven at once: 21 wheat seeds for an empty composter. A smaller surplus waits.

Level seven still matures for the original twenty ticks. At level eight a resident collects one real bone meal and empties the composter. Turning automatic composting off stops new input while mature bone meal can still be collected.

With Restore grass enabled, real bone meal can replenish a safe, flat 15 by 15 grass patch over non-grass soil. The full native growth footprint must belong to this area. Missing bone meal, a small patch or unsafe bounds makes restoration wait.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_spit.hea: The shawarma spit: real power, separate halves and a safe grip
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_spit.tex: Mark either half to register one kitchen station. Each half holds its own native batch of up to eight matching campfire ingredients.
An order uses an empty half and preserves food already placed by a player. The colony tracks only the ingredients it actually accepted.
The real redstone signal drives the native cooking clock. Removing power pauses the same batch; it does not turn raw food into a finished meal.

After native cooking finishes, the booked resident uses a real kitchen knife to collect its own batch safely. This grip protects only that task; it does not grant general fire immunity or switch off external power.
The actual cooked portions enter colony logistics once. Cancellation and reload recover accepted food without spending the same raw ingredients again.
The steamer: layers, a top lid and real heat
A continuous column is one kitchen station. A half block holds four portions, a full block holds eight; heat passes upward only through full blocks, to at most four block levels.
The task reserves an entirely empty block and places several real ingredients in one native interaction. Food in other blocks stays with its original owner.
The reachable top lid closes using the native lid rule. Lower blocks are covered by the stack above them; a half block below another steamer cannot pass its heat upward.
A real heat source is still required. When it disappears, an owned batch cools down through the native ticker and waits for heat to return.
Collection waits until every owned portion is actually steamed. The native take-out moves all food in that block, so the task never mixes its ingredients with a player's slots.
The real portions are delivered once, and a lid changed by this task returns to its original state. Empty or changed batches are refused instead of accidentally dismantling a steamer layer.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_teapot.h: Brewing tea: a real bucket, a tea bag and twelve cups
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_teapot.t: Mark a teapot and order the finished tea. Each native recipe brews twelve portions, so the plan also supplies twelve real empty cups and leaves an accessible place to serve them.

Native filling transfers a real bucket of the recipe's fluid and returns its empty container. Water teas and milk tea use their actual different fluids; the pot is not filled by changing a display value.

The actual ingredient then enters the pot. Its native grace period and brewing timer both require real heat. Removing heat pauses the same accepted batch, and reload does not charge another bag or bucket.

After brewing finishes, the real filled pot is picked up. The resident places one of its own cups, pours one portion from the pot's actual stored result, and takes the real filled cup. Player cup positions are never overwritten.

This repeats for all twelve actual portions. A failed serving transaction restores the finished pot and returns only its unspent cups; it never leaves extra filled cups while also refunding their containers.

The one real, now-empty pot returns to its original station. The twelve filled cups and the empty fluid bucket enter logistics once; neither a duplicate pot nor twelve leftover empty cups are created.

Normal tea orders use matching native recipes. Only an explicit Mystery Tea order brews an unmatched ingredient: 200 ticks of input waiting, then 2,400 ticks of native brewing with heat. It yields four real cups instead of twelve, so prepare four empty cups.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_tools.he: Shared kitchen tools: borrow for a task and return them
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_tools.te: Mark a kitchenware rack as a store. Its two real slots hold one supported tool each; ordinary stores remain available when the rack is full.
Idle crafting residents do not each fetch a knife. A task borrows the knife, shovel or sickle it actually needs, and keeps that same physical tool until its work is over.
One knife means one active borrower. Another task waits while it is busy or being carried; waiting never creates a second knife.

The returned tool goes to an allowed rack first, then an ordinary store, keeping its name, enchantments and native wear. Only after the old tool breaks or becomes unavailable, with no usable shared tool or delivery on the way, is one replacement requested.

Only when the colony truly has no suitable tool and no real supply already underway does it ask for one replacement. Tool crafting happens before the food task, so the first crafting resident can make the first knife.

For two parallel tasks, set a knife maintain order with both its minimum and target at two. Actual borrowed knives promised back to that store still count, so borrowing them does not manufacture spare copies.
The colony's Tools list still controls which tools may be used. An empty allowed list permits none; more residents alone never raises the shared stock target.
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_tray.hea: The bamboo tray: exposure, real drips and reversible batches
folkways_cookery.ponder.cookery_tray.tex: Register a bamboo tray and order its real drying or wetting product. A task reserves one empty slot; food placed by a player in the other slots stays in place.
Drying needs the native clear exposure and dry weather. An opaque roof pauses progress; an open column or suitable clear glass allows the same real batch to continue.
The tray advances on its own native timer. The task waits for the actual completion flag instead of inventing dried leaves or skipping the recipe duration.
Wetting uses actual rain or a water-fed stalactite. Many conversions are reversible, so a later weather change may process the material again until the requested product is collected.

Only the actual owned result is taken. Cancellation and reload preserve accepted materials; changed player contents are refused without refunding or duplicating them. Dried leaves can then feed real tea-bag crafting and brewing.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.header: Tavern: from the vineyard to a glass of wine
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_1: Mark a rectangular grape plot and choose grapevines. Supply trellises and grapevine plants: residents build four corner posts, each four blocks high, then a pergola over the plot five blocks above the soil.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_2: Residents plant the vines at the feet of the finished posts. The vines grow over the pergola and hang grapes underneath; residents pick the ripe grapes. Leave room around the plot to work.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_3: Register a pressing tub and a Tavern barrel as kitchen stations, allow the crafting trade and order wine. Residents press eight grapes into a juice bucket. Supply buckets and empty wine bottles as well.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_4: The barrel takes four juice buckets through its top. Build a route onto it, such as a stepladder. Keep a closed tap on its side and solid ground beneath the bottle spot; after fermentation residents set out, fill and collect the bottles one at a time.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_5: Bar cabinets hold the bottles themselves and can be stocked through delivery orders when registered as storage. Bar counters in a dining area are stocked automatically from its drink list. Choose wine there and keep the counter reachable.
folkways_cookery.ponder.tavern.text_6: After a table meal, a diner can fetch a bottle from the counter. A chair beside the counter also lets a resident sit for a drink. Drinking gives the wine's own effects and leaves the empty bottle behind.
